rows: Establishing a democratic system and constitution

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Democracy faces three fundamental types of challenges: foundational challenge, challenge of expansion, and challenge of deepening of democracy.
The foundational challenge involves establishing democratic institutions, removing non-democratic regimes, and ensuring civilian control over the military.
The challenge of expansion requires applying democratic principles across all regions, social groups, and institutions including local governments.
The deepening of democracy focuses on strengthening democratic institutions and practices that enable active public participation and control.
Effective democratic reforms rely primarily on political activists, parties, popular movements, and politically conscious citizens rather than legal mandates alone.
Differentiate clearly between Foundational, Expansion, and Deepening challenges for UPSC Governance and Polity mains questions.
The Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005 is frequently cited as a model reform that empowers citizens to control corruption.
Legal-constitutional changes alone are insufficient; grass-root political participation and institutional accountability are essential for democratic reform.
